title: MCPs & connectors
content:
## What is MCP?

The **Model Context Protocol** (MCP) is an open standard that lets AI agents discover and use external tools, data sources, and services. Instead of hard-coding integrations, agents speak MCP to dynamically fetch schemas, call functions, and retrieve context from any MCP-compatible server.

In Emergent, the build agent uses MCP connectors to pull real-time data (APIs, databases, file systems) and invoke external actions during code generation, testing, and deployment.

<Note>
MCP servers expose **tools** (callable functions), **resources** (readable data), and **prompts** (reusable templates). Emergent's agent discovers these capabilities automatically when you register a server.
</Note>

## Using an MCP connector

An **MCP connector** bridges Emergent's build agent to an external service. When you register a connector, the agent can:

- **Read resources** — fetch schemas, documentation, or live data (e.g., rows from a Notion database, files from Google Drive).
- **Call tools** — trigger actions like sending a Slack message, creating a Jira ticket, or querying a REST API.
- **Inject context** — use prompts defined by the server to guide code generation.

Common use cases:

| Connector type | Example | What it enables |
|----------------|---------|-----------------|
| Database | PostgreSQL MCP | Read schemas, run queries, validate migrations |
| SaaS API | Stripe MCP | Fetch product catalog, create checkout sessions |
| File system | Local filesystem MCP | Access project templates, reference documents |
| Communication | Slack MCP | Send notifications, read channel history |

<Tip>
Third-party MCP servers are often published as npm packages or Docker images. Check [modelcontextprotocol.io](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) or GitHub for community-maintained servers.
</Tip>

## Emergent as an MCP server

Emergent itself exposes an **MCP interface** on port `8013` (local) or via a public endpoint when deployed. This lets you use Emergent as a tool from other AI clients—Claude Desktop, Cursor, or custom agents.

**Available tools** (example):

- `emergent.create_app` — start a new app from a prompt.
- `emergent.deploy` — trigger deployment of a workspace.
- `emergent.get_logs` — retrieve build or runtime logs.

To connect from Claude Desktop or another MCP client, configure the server URL and any required API key in the client's MCP settings. Emergent will return its tool schemas, and the client can invoke them like any other MCP tool.

<Info>
Self-hosting users can customize the exposed tools by editing the MCP server configuration in `config/mcp.json` (see installation docs for details).
</Info>

## Registering a custom MCP server

To give the build agent access to a custom or third-party MCP server:

<Steps>
<Step title="Prepare the server endpoint">
Your MCP server must listen on a reachable address (localhost for local dev, or a public HTTPS URL for cloud). Ensure it implements the MCP specification (`initialize`, `tools/list`, `tools/call`, etc.).
</Step>

<Step title="Add the server to your workspace config">
In the Emergent workspace, open **Settings → Integrations → MCP Servers** and click **Add Server**. Provide:

- **Name** — a unique identifier (e.g., `my-postgres-db`).
- **Endpoint** — the base URL or `stdio` command (e.g., `http://localhost:8012` or `npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-postgres`).
- **Auth** (if required) — API key, bearer token, or environment variable reference.
- **Visibility** — `private` (workspace-only) or `public` (shared across your account).
</Step>

<Step title="Save and test connection">
Click **Save**. Emergent will call the server's `initialize` method and cache the list of tools and resources. Check the **Connection Status** indicator—green means the agent can reach the server.
</Step>

<Step title="Use discovered tools in chat">
Registered tools appear in the agent's tool palette. When you describe a task that matches a tool's schema, the agent will propose calling it. You can also reference the server explicitly:

> "Use the `my-postgres-db` connector to read the users table schema and generate a GraphQL API."

</Step>
</Steps>

<Warning>
**Port 8012** is the default for stdio-launched MCP servers in Emergent's local environment. If your server binds to a different port, specify the full URL in the endpoint field.
</Warning>

### Public vs. private servers

- **Private** — only the current workspace can use this server. Config stored in workspace metadata.
- **Public** — any workspace in your account can discover and call the server. Config stored in your global MCP registry.

Use private for project-specific databases or credentials; use public for shared services (company Slack, internal APIs).

### Tool discovery and caching

Emergent caches tool schemas for **24 hours** after the first successful connection. If you update the server's tools (add a new function, change parameters), click **Refresh Schema** in the MCP Servers list to force a re-discovery. The agent will re-fetch the tool list and update its knowledge.

<Tip>
For rapidly evolving servers, enable **Auto-refresh on job start** in the server settings. The agent will re-discover tools at the beginning of each build job, ensuring it always sees the latest API.
</Tip>
